item.base_system: WMoTaNbV alloy produced via PBF-LB/M with parameter set A (High scan speed, low energy density)
item.intervention: Used parameter set A: 600 W laser power, 800 mm/s scan speed, 120 µm hatch distance (125 J/mm³ volumetric energy density)
item.processing: PBF-LB/M on AconityMINI machine, 6 mm cubic samples on Mo substrate
item.test_conditions: Microstructural analysis via SEM, EBSD, EDS
item.structure_change: Larger structure size, more distinct secondary dendrites, considerable cracks perpendicular to build direction, presence of undissolved tungsten particles
item.attributed_mechanism: Higher growth rates R and lower temperature gradients G favor columnar dendritic solidification; high scan speed leads to less dissolution of high melting W particles
quotes: Parameter set PBF-LB/M A features a larger structure size and more distinct secondary dendrites, while the material processed with parameter set PBF-LB/M B solidifies in an almost cellular structure with only a few secondary dendrites.
PBF-LB/M A results in considerably smaller cracks than PBF-LB/M B but contains undissolved powder particles which were identified as tungsten particles by EDS measurements.
The microhardness of the PBF-LB/M A sample with the coarser structure is 561 ± 17 HV0.1 (n = 9).

item.base_system: WMoTaNbV alloy produced via PBF-LB/M with parameter set B (Low scan speed, high energy density)
item.intervention: Used parameter set B: 100 W laser power, 100 mm/s scan speed, 45 µm hatch distance (889 J/mm³ volumetric energy density)
item.processing: PBF-LB/M on AconityMINI machine, 6 mm cubic samples on Mo substrate
item.test_conditions: Microstructural analysis via SEM, EBSD, EDS
item.structure_change: Almost cellular structure with few secondary dendrites, fewer undissolved particles, wider cracks compared to Set A
item.attributed_mechanism: Higher volumetric energy density and slower scan speed facilitate dissolution of high melting W particles; higher energy input causes higher internal stress leading to wider cracks
quotes: Parameter set PBF-LB/M B comprises a considerably lower scan speed (100 mm/s vs. 800 mm/s) but, despite the lower laser power, a higher volumetric energy density (889 J/mm 3 vs. 125 J/mm 3 ) than parameter set PBF-LB/M A.
This facilitates the dissolution of the high melting W particles, thus leading to less undissolved particles as shown in Figure 2.
The microhardness of the PBF-LB/M B sample is 614 ± 21 HV0.1 (n = 9).

item.base_system: WMoTaNbV alloy produced by PBF-LB/M (Set B)
item.intervention: Analysis of grain size compared to vacuum arc melted samples
item.processing: EBSD measurements on PBF-LB/M B sample
item.test_conditions: Comparison with literature data from Senkov et al.
item.structure_change: Average grain size of 16.3 µm (PBF-LB/M) vs. 80 µm (vacuum arc melted)
item.property_change: Grain size reduced by a factor of more than four
item.attributed_mechanism: Smaller grain size attributed to high cooling rates in the range of 10^6 K/s during the PBF-LB/M process
quotes: The average grain size determined by the linear intercept method is 16.3 µm.
This is more than a factor of four smaller than the 80 µm reported by Senkov et al. for vacuum arc molten samples.
The smaller grain size can be attributed to the high cooling rates in the range of 10 6 K/s during the PBF-LB/M process.

item.intervention: Comparison of element distribution between interdendritic and intradendritic areas

item.property_change: Homogeneity of element distribution achieved is very good compared to vacuum arc molten samples
item.attributed_mechanism: Higher solidification rates and temperature gradients inherent to PBF-LB/M mitigate segregation
quotes: Nb and Mo are almost equally distributed between inter- and intradendritic regions, while Ta and especially W are predominantly located in the intradendritic areas.

item.processing: Optical microscopy and SEM analysis of polished microsections
item.test_conditions: Comparison of crack patterns between parameter sets A and B
item.structure_change: Cracks mostly perpendicular to build direction; wider cracks in Set B samples
item.property_change: Cracking observed in both samples despite high density
item.attributed_mechanism: Cracking caused by internal stress induced by PBF-LB/M and insufficient ductility at lower temperatures; wider cracks in Set B due to higher volumetric energy density and smaller hatch distance causing higher stress values
quotes: Instead, cracking of the already solidified material due to internal stress induced by the PBF-LB/M process and an insufficient ductility of the material at lower temperatures is assumed to be the cause for the cracks.

The different crack patterns in dependence of the parameter set PBF-LB/M A and PBF-LB/M B with wider cracks in the PBF-LB/M B samples are a result of the smaller hatch distance (45 µm vs. 120 µm) and the higher volumetric energy density applied (889 J/mm 3 vs. 125 J/mm 3 ) compared to parameter set PBF-LB/M A.

item.intervention: Comparison of solidification modes between parameter sets A and B
item.test_conditions: Analysis of growth rates (R) and temperature gradients (G)
item.structure_change: Set A: Columnar dendritic; Set B: Cellular solidification
item.property_change: Different microhardness values resulting from different solidification modes
item.attributed_mechanism: Higher growth rates R and lower temperature gradients G favor columnar dendritic solidification (Set A); lower growth rates R and higher temperature gradients G favor cellular solidification (Set B)
quotes: Based on the process parameters it is safe to assume that the material is subject to higher growth rates R when processed with parameter set PBF-LB/M A compared to parameter set PBF-LB/M B.

While higher growth rates R and lower temperature gradients G in the liquid favor a columnar dendritic solidification, lower growth rates R and higher temperature gradients in the liquid G favor cellular solidification.
These different solidification modes also affect the material properties.

item.intervention: Use of milled V-powder instead of spherical V-powder
item.processing: Mixing of W, Mo, Ta, Nb (spherical) and V (milled) powders
item.structure_change: Sufficient recoatability achieved despite irregular shaped V-powder having lower flowability
item.property_change: Successful manufacturing of samples with high relative density

The irregular shaped, milled V-powder has a lower flowability than spherical powder.
Preliminary recoating test nevertheless proved a sufficient recoatability of the blend for all five powders.

item.intervention: Comparison of interlayer boundaries in microstructure
item.test_conditions: Analysis of temperature gradients and growth rates at melt pool contours
item.structure_change: Coarser structures at interlayer boundaries compared to inner regions of melt pools
item.property_change: Demonstrates sensitivity of alloy to solidification conditions
item.attributed_mechanism: Temperature gradients in the liquid and growth rates are smaller at the outer contours of the meltpool compared to the inner regions
quotes: As visible in Figure 4 inter layer boundaries are clearly distinguished by coarser structures.
According to [ [51] ] temperature gradients in the liquid and growth rates are smaller at the outer contours of the meltpool compared to the inner regions, explaining the coarser structures.
This demonstrates the sensitivity of the alloy to the solidification conditions and offers the chance to influence material properties by adjusting the PBF-LB/M process conditions/parameters.

item.processing: Suggestion of high temperature build-platform heating (>600 °C) or high purity powder
item.test_conditions: Theoretical proposal based on observed cracking
item.property_change: Avoidance of cracks caused by internal stress and low ductility
item.attributed_mechanism: High temperature heating or low O/N content powder would mitigate cracking caused by internal stress and brittle grain boundaries
quotes: Based on these findings, a high temperature (>600 °C) build-platform heating device and/or high purity powder with low O and N content are suggested for crack-free PBF-LB/M of WMoTaNbV.
The brittle grain boundaries in combination with the internal stress induced during PBF-LB/M consequently lead to cracking of the samples during processing.

item.intervention: In-situ alloy formation from elemental powders vs. pre-alloyed powder
item.processing: Mixing of elemental powders and PBF-LB/M processing
item.test_conditions: Feasibility study of in-situ alloy formation
item.structure_change: Achievement of single bcc-phase and high relative density without pre-alloyed powder
item.property_change: Demonstrates feasibility of in-situ alloy formation for refractory metal HEAs
item.attributed_mechanism: In-situ alloy formation avoids expensive atomization of pre-alloyed powder and supports material development and high throughput investigations
quotes: In-situ alloy formation from mixtures of easily available elemental powders is employed to avoid an expensive atomization of pre-alloyed powder.

It is shown that PBF-LB/M of W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is in general possible and that a complete fusion of the powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles is achievable by in-situ alloy formation during PBF-LB/M when selecting favorable process parameter combinations.

The possibility of in-situ alloy formation by PBF-LB/M could therefore be a valuable tool to facilitate high throughput investigations that are key to identify application-relevant alloys within the vast number of possible alloy compositions inherent to the high entropy concept.
